# 葬書

**ID:** KR3g0020
**Custom ID:** ZB3g0021
**Source:** 四庫全書 文淵閣版, V808.2, p11
**Extent:** 1 卷

## Authors / Editors
- 郭璞 (晉朝) 撰 276 - 324
- 吳澄 (元朝) 刪定

**Editions:** WYG

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A 1-juan foundational text of the Chinese geomantic tradition for **tomb siting** (*xiàngmù* 相墓) — sister-discipline to the residence-siting tradition exemplified by [KR3g0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3g/KR3g0019) *Zháijīng*. The work is universally cited as the foundational text of the *Zàngshū* / *Zàngjīng* tradition, but its actual textual-historical situation is complex.

The Sìkù 提要 makes a thorough textual-critical case:

(a) **The Zhōu-Hàn evidence**: tomb-siting practice is *not* documented in pre-Hàn Confucian sources. The Zhōu-li *Zhǒngrén* and *Mùdàfū* offices indicate that ancient burial used clan-based collective sites without site-selection.

(b) **The Hàn evidence**: the *Hànshū Yìwén zhì* groups *xíngfǎ* (form-method) — including residence-siting, person-siting, animal-siting — together with no separate tomb-siting branch. So while geomancy as a category emerged in the Hàn, *tomb-siting* per se was not yet specialized.

(c) **The Eastern-Hàn / Tang evidence**: the *Hòu-Hànshū Yuán Ān zhuàn*'s anecdote about the three students directing Yuán Ān's father to an auspicious burial site documents the practice's emergence in the Eastern Hàn. The Tang-end-period catalogs list a *Zàngshū dìmài jīng* and a *Zàngshū wǔyīn* — both anonymous, neither attributed to Guō Pú.

(d) **The Sòng emergence**: only the *Sòng zhì* records "*Guō Pú's *Zàngshū* 1 *juàn**" — i.e., the *Guō Pú* attribution dates to the Sòng. The Sòng-period text is what underlies all subsequent transmission.

(e) **The Cài Yuándìng critical revision**: the late-Sòng text proliferated to "*twenty pieces*"; Cài Yuándìng 蔡元定 ([蔡元定](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%94%A1%E5%85%83%E5%AE%9A)) "*sickened of its weed-and-confusion, deleted twelve pieces, preserving eight*". His son Cài Shěn ([蔡沈](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%94%A1%E6%B2%88)) was Zhū Xī's principal disciple, locating Cài Yuándìng's redaction within the Cheng-Zhū school's text-critical lineage.

(f) **The Wú Chéng further refinement**: Wú Chéng 吳澄 ([吳澄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%90%B3%E6%BE%84)) further subdivided Cài's eight-piece recension into *Inner Chapter* (*nèipiān*, the most pure-and-correct), *Outer Chapter* (*wàipiān*, mixed pure-and-coarse), and *Mixed Chapter* (*zápiān*, the coarse-and-impure that should be deleted but is kept tentatively). The present transmitted text follows Wú Chéng's three-chapter division.

(g) **The Liú Zézhāng commentary**: Liú Zézhāng 劉則章 of Xīnyú 新喻 received Wú Chéng's recension directly and produced the now-standard commentary; the *Sìkù* recension's commentary attribution to Liú Zézhāng is uncertain.

(h) **The title transmission**: the Sòng-period title was *Zàngshū* (Burial Book); subsequent geomancy-promoters renamed it *Zàngjīng* (Burial Classic) to enhance its authority. Máo Jìn's 毛晉 *Jígǔgé* edition uses the inflated title; the Sìkù editors restore the original *Zàngshū*.

The work's geomantic content develops the foundational concepts of the tomb-siting tradition: *qì* 氣 (vital pneuma) flowing through the earth; *lóng* 龍 (dragon = mountain ridges as channels of *qì*); *xué* 穴 (acupoint = the site at which *qì* emerges, where the tomb should be placed); *shā* 砂 (surrounding mountains protecting the site); *shuǐ* 水 (water flow patterns auspiciously surrounding the site).

For the parallel residence-siting foundational text, see [KR3g0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3g/KR3g0019) *Zháijīng*. For the principal Tang-period geomantic technical works (the *Yáng Yúnsōng* tradition), see [KR3g0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3g/KR3g0021) *Hànlóng jīng* and the related works. For the textual-critical figures, see [蔡元定](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%94%A1%E5%85%83%E5%AE%9A) (Cài Yuándìng), [吳澄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%90%B3%E6%BE%84) (Wú Chéng).
